The father went away. His son grew up and became a warrior, and in his youth he grew strong. Then the father arrived with a troop, and the warrior stepped against him: "Warrior, who is your father?" "My father went away. Men say: 'He vanished.'" "I am your father." "I do not trust you. Lift your spear!" Then he said: "I shall strike down my son, or my son will strike me down." Man, wake up and yoke the cattle with the yoke! Wife, rise, milk the cattle, heat the water and cook the grain! Sons and daughters, do not lie down! Old man, sit at the door and look at the path. The shepherd led the sheep, the man yoked the cattle, and the wife milked them.

Why do you speak to the fire? The fire is a god. Without him the bronze does not melt. What do you say to him? Fire, burn strongly, and do not burn my hands! Does he hear you? He hears me. Look! The bronze is flowing. Now pour it into the stone!

h₁éḱwos sruméni tḱéyt wĺ̥kʷos-kʷe tóm gʷémt. só wiHrṓy wérh₁t. tóm wĺ̥kʷom noḱéye. só h₂éǵt. h₁yód me wéǵʰēsi tóm noḱéyōh₂. nu só tóm wéǵʰet só-kʷe tóm gʷrúh₁ kélh₂t. nu só wĺ̥kʷos séngʷt só-kʷe stéwdt. nu só h₁éḱwos tósmey wéwket. l̥h₁dʰí me. só wiHrós tóm ne léh₁t kʷékʷlōy-kʷe tóm yunégt. nu só h₁éḱwos tósyo kʷékʷlom déwkti. h₁yós wiHróm wéǵʰeti só wiHrós tóm h₂éǵeti.

A horse dwelt by a stream, and a wolf came to him. He said to a man: "Kill the wolf!" He said: "If you carry me, I will kill it." Then he carried him, and he struck it with a spear. Then the wolf fell, and it grew cold. Then the horse said to him: "Let me go!" The man did not let him go, and he joined him to a wagon. Now the horse draws his wagon. Whoever carries a man, the man drives him.

Wolf and the two brothers made a pledge. Wolf spoke: "Father Sky, listen to my word! I shall not steal the cattle of the brothers. If I steal them, may Perkʷunos strike me!"
